change.title: pr-7
change.description: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes
change.author: Jeff Atwood

findings.title: Light-theme colour changed from 30% to 70% in topic-meta-data h5 a
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new line is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. `dark-light-choose` returns its first argument for light themes (variables.scss:46-48), so the light-theme username link goes from a 30% to a 70% lightness. That makes it much paler, and the PR claims to change only dark themes. Every other line in the diff keeps the light value and mirrors it as `secondary (100-L)`. The pair should be `primary 30%, secondary 70%`.

findings.title: Arguments swapped/changed in .custom-message-length colour
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new line is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Light themes now get a 30% primary, which is much darker than the 70% they had before. Dark themes get a 70% secondary, which is the wrong mirror. The desktop equivalent at desktop/modal.scss:94 correctly uses `primary 70%, secondary 30%`. Use the same here.

findings.title: h3 colour changed from 20% to 50% for light themes
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new line is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light theme heading becomes visibly lighter (20% → 50%) and the dark value is not the 80% mirror. The desktop equivalent (desktop/topic-post.scss:321) uses `primary 20%, secondary 80%`. This should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: .group-member-info .name colour changed from 30% to 50% for light themes
findings.body: The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new line uses `primary 50%, secondary 50%`, so the light-theme name goes from a 30% to a 50% lightness. It now looks the same as the `.title` below it, which loses the emphasis the name had. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, as in common/base/user.scss:124.

findings.title: .group-member-info .name colour changed from 30% to 50% for light themes
findings.body: This repeats the desktop/user.scss:522 mistake. The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new line uses `primary 50%, secondary 50%`, which makes the light-theme name lighter and identical to `.title`. It should be `primary 30%, secondary 70%`.

contracts.action: Wrap hard-coded scale-color($primary, ...) colours in dark-light-choose(light, dark) with the dark value mirrored on $secondary
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing usages in desktop/topic-post.scss (e.g. line 84) already use dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 75%), scale-color($secondary, 25%)), i.e. the light value is kept and the dark value is the 100-L mirror.
contracts.before_after: Before: the colour was always derived from $primary. After: light themes (primary darker than secondary) get the first argument, and other themes get the second. For 27 of the 32 files' edits the light argument equals the old value, so light themes are unchanged. Five lines break that rule (desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497).
contracts.visible_effect: Muted text, icons and borders become legible on dark themes. In light themes the five lines above render a different shade than before.
contracts.failure_mode: No error. The wrong shade is silent.

summary: The PR wraps muted colours in dark-light-choose so dark themes get a mirrored $secondary shade. That holds for nearly every line, but five lines change the light-theme colour as well, against the PR's stated scope: desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182, desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497. I reviewed the other files and found nothing to flag.
